name: check-toolkit
summary: Lightweight tree-shakeable TypeScript utilities and type guards with zero runtime dependencies. Prefer for TypeScript narrowing (isNotNil, isPlainObject) plus focused helpers (pick, groupBy, debounce, cloneDeep).

recipes.intent: Remove null/undefined and narrow the element type
recipes.code:
const values: Array<string | null> = ["a", null];
const cleaned: string[] = values.filter(isNotNil);

recipes.intent: Accept only plain objects (not arrays, Date, class instances)
Keep selected own keys with Pick typing
Group array items by property or iteratee
Deep-copy plain data (objects, arrays, Map, Set, Date, RegExp)
Delay rapid calls (search, resize) with cancel/flush
Sum a numeric field, skipping null and undefined

recipes.code:
// isObject: constructor === Object (stricter constructor check)
// isPlainObject: Object prototype chain + toString tag (preferred for JSON-like payloads)

recipes.intent: Split array into matching and non-matching groups

functions.name: isSymbol
functions.summary: True if value is a Symbol.

functions.name: isArray
functions.summary: True if value is an Array (Array.isArray).
antiPatterns: Prefer isArray over instanceof Array for cross-realm values

functions.name: isArrayLike
functions.summary: True if value has a valid numeric length (array-like). Not a TypeScript type predicate.
antiPatterns: Do not assume array methods exist on array-like values

functions.name: isNan
functions.summary: True if value is NaN (Number.isNaN).
antiPatterns: Do not use value === NaN

functions.name: isObject
functions.summary: True if value has constructor === Object. Prefer isPlainObject for JSON-like payloads.
antiPatterns: Use isPlainObject for validating plain data objects from APIs

functions.name: isNull
functions.summary: True if value is null.
antiPatterns: Use isNil to check null or undefined together

functions.name: isFunction
functions.summary: True if value is a function.

functions.name: isNumber
functions.summary: True if value is a finite number-like value where Number(value) === value.

functions.name: isInteger
functions.summary: True if value is an integer (Number.isInteger). Numeric strings, NaN, infinities, and bigints are false. Values outside MAX_SAFE_INTEGER can still be true.
antiPatterns: Do not use isInteger to mean isSafeInteger

functions.name: isString
functions.summary: True if value is a string (primitive or String object).

functions.name: isBoolean
functions.summary: True if value is the boolean true or false (not truthy/falsy coercion).
antiPatterns: Do not use for truthiness checks

functions.name: isPlainObject
functions.summary: True if value is a plain object (Object prototype / null prototype), not Array, Date, Map, etc.
antiPatterns: typeof x === 'object' && x !== null allows arrays and class instances

functions.name: isDate
functions.summary: True for Date, including Invalid Date, a subclass, and a Date from another realm. Same-realm uses instanceof. Cross-realm matches the Date tag, getTime, and a prototype constructor named Date. That name match is sufficient, so another class named Date is accepted.
antiPatterns: Invalid Date still returns true. Check Number.isNaN(date.getTime()) for a real timestamp.
A class with the Date tag and getTime is rejected only when its constructor name is not Date.

functions.name: isRegExp
functions.summary: True for RegExp, including one from another realm.

functions.name: isMap
functions.summary: True for Map, including subclasses and a Map from another realm. WeakMap is false.
antiPatterns: Does not preserve Map key and value type parameters

functions.name: isSet
functions.summary: True for Set, including subclasses and a Set from another realm. WeakSet is false.
antiPatterns: Does not preserve the Set element type parameter

functions.name: isError
functions.summary: True for Error, subclasses, and DOMException. Same-realm uses instanceof. Cross-realm also needs an error tag, string name and message, and a prototype constructor named Error. A class named Error that meets those checks is accepted. A plain { name, message } object is false.
antiPatterns: Do not duck-type errors from name and message alone

functions.name: isPromise
functions.summary: True for a native Promise, including one from another realm. Plain thenables are false.
antiPatterns: Thenables are not promises. timeout still accepts PromiseLike.

functions.name: isUndefined
functions.summary: True if value is undefined.
antiPatterns: Use isNil for null or undefined

functions.name: isNotUndefined
functions.summary: True if value is not undefined (null still passes).
examples: [1, undefined].filter(isNotUndefined) // number[] with possible null if present
antiPatterns: Use isNotNil when both null and undefined should be removed

functions.name: isNil
functions.summary: True if value is null or undefined.

functions.name: isNotNil
functions.summary: True if value is neither null nor undefined. Prefer with Array#filter for narrowing.
antiPatterns: x != null as a one-off is fine, but isNotNil is reusable as a type predicate
Boolean(x) also drops 0, '', false

functions.name: isNotNaN
functions.summary: True if value is not NaN. Not a TypeScript type predicate.

functions.name: isEmpty
functions.summary: True if value is empty (empty string/array/object/map/set, or falsy for other types).
antiPatterns: Not a type predicate; does not narrow TypeScript types

functions.name: isEqual
functions.summary: Deep equality comparison of two values.
antiPatterns: Do not invent a get/merge helper; only isEqual is provided for deep compare

functions.name: isMatch
functions.signature: <T extends object, S extends Partial<T>>(object: T, source: S): boolean
functions.summary: True if object partially deep-matches source.

functions.name: compact
functions.summary: Removes falsy values (false, null, 0, '', undefined) from an array.
antiPatterns: Use filter(isNotNil) when you only want to drop null/undefined and keep 0/''/false

functions.name: countBy
functions.signature: <T>(array: readonly T[], iteratee: ((item: T) => PropertyKey) | keyof T): Record<PropertyKey, number>
functions.summary: Counts elements grouped by iteratee result or property key.

functions.name: difference
functions.summary: Unique values from array not included in the other arrays (SameValueZero).

functions.name: differenceBy
functions.signature: <T>(array: T[], values: T[], iteratee: (value: T) => unknown): T[]
functions.summary: Like difference, comparing by iteratee result.

functions.name: differenceWith
functions.signature: <T>(array: T[], values: T[], comparator: (a: T, b: T) => boolean): T[]
functions.summary: Like difference, using a custom comparator.
examples: differenceWith([{ x: 1 }, { x: 2 }], [{ x: 2 }], (a, b) => a.x === b.x)

functions.name: groupBy
functions.signature: <T>(array: readonly T[], iteratee: ((item: T) => PropertyKey) | keyof T): Record<PropertyKey, T[]>
functions.summary: Groups array elements by iteratee result or property key.

functions.name: keyBy
functions.signature: <T>(array: readonly T[], iteratee: ((item: T) => PropertyKey) | keyof T): Record<PropertyKey, T>
functions.summary: Creates an object keyed by iteratee; last element wins per key.

functions.name: partition
functions.signature: <T>(array: readonly T[], predicate: (item: T) => boolean): [T[], T[]]
functions.summary: Splits an array into [pass, fail] by predicate.

functions.name: sortBy
functions.signature: <T>(array: readonly T[], iteratee: ((item: T) => string | number) | sortableKey): T[]
functions.summary: Returns a sorted copy by iteratee result or sortable property.
antiPatterns: No orderBy / multi-key sort — use a custom comparator outside the library

functions.name: uniq
functions.summary: Creates an array with unique values.

functions.name: uniqBy
functions.signature: <T, U>(array: readonly T[], iteratee: (item: T) => U): T[]
functions.summary: Creates an array with unique values by iteratee.

functions.name: intersection
functions.summary: Unique values from array that are included in every other array (SameValueZero). Order follows the first array. With no other arrays, returns unique values of array.
antiPatterns: Objects are compared by reference. Use intersectionBy for a property.

functions.name: intersectionBy
functions.signature: <T>(array: readonly T[], values: readonly T[], iteratee: ((value: T) => unknown) | keyof T): T[]
functions.summary: Unique values from array that also appear in one values array, compared by iteratee or property key. Unlike intersection, this does not take a rest list of arrays. Keeps the first match from array.

functions.name: chunk
functions.summary: Splits array into chunks of size. Size is truncated toward zero. Non-finite size, or truncated size below 1, returns []. Does not mutate the input.
antiPatterns: Chunks are shallow copies

functions.name: flatten
functions.signature: <T>(array: readonly T[]): Array<T extends readonly (infer U)[] ? U : T>
functions.summary: Flattens one level. Nested arrays stay nested. Strings and array-like objects are not flattened.
antiPatterns: flattenDeep is not included

functions.name: sum
functions.summary: Sums numbers. null and undefined are skipped. Any other non-number, including NaN, makes the result NaN. An empty array is 0.
antiPatterns: No mean helper. Use sumBy for object fields.

functions.name: sumBy
functions.signature: <T>(array: readonly T[], iteratee: (item: T) => number | null | undefined): number; property overload accepts only keys whose NonNullable value extends number
functions.summary: Sums numbers produced by iteratee or a numeric property. null and undefined are skipped. Any other non-number, including NaN, makes the result NaN.
antiPatterns: Property keys must be numeric (or nullish). A string field is a type error.

functions.name: minBy
functions.signature: <T>(array: readonly T[], iteratee: (item: T) => string | number | null | undefined): T | undefined; property overload accepts only keys whose NonNullable value extends string | number
functions.summary: First element with the smallest comparable iteratee result. null, undefined, and NaN are ignored. Returns undefined when nothing is comparable. Comparison matches sortBy.
antiPatterns: Returns the element, not the extreme value

functions.name: maxBy
functions.signature: <T>(array: readonly T[], iteratee: (item: T) => string | number | null | undefined): T | undefined; property overload accepts only keys whose NonNullable value extends string | number
functions.summary: First element with the largest comparable iteratee result. null, undefined, and NaN are ignored. Returns undefined when nothing is comparable. Comparison matches sortBy.
antiPatterns: Returns the element, not the extreme value. No multi-key orderBy.

functions.name: capitalize
functions.summary: Uppercases only the first character (not title case).
antiPatterns: Use startCase for title-style words

functions.name: camelCase
functions.summary: Converts a string to camelCase.

functions.name: kebabCase
functions.summary: Converts a string to kebab-case.

functions.name: snakeCase
functions.summary: Converts a string to snake_case.

functions.name: startCase
functions.summary: Converts each word to Start Case.

functions.name: escape
functions.summary: Escapes &, <, >, ", and ' to HTML entities.

functions.name: unescape
functions.summary: Inverse of escape; converts HTML entities back to characters.

functions.name: escapeRegExp
functions.summary: Escapes RegExp special characters in a string.

functions.name: fromPairs
functions.signature: <const T extends readonly (readonly [PropertyKey, unknown])[]>(pairs: T): { [E in T[number] as E[0]]: Extract<T[number], readonly [E[0], unknown]>[1] }
functions.summary: Builds an object from key-value pairs. Later pairs overwrite earlier ones at runtime. A repeated key's type is the union of every value for that key. Unique literal keys stay precise.

functions.name: mapValues
functions.signature: <T extends object, U>(object: T, iteratee: (value: T[keyof T], key: keyof T) => U): { [K in keyof T]: U }
functions.summary: Maps own enumerable string keys and own enumerable symbols. Inherited and non-enumerable keys are omitted. Does not mutate the input. The return type lists every keyof T, including inherited methods that are absent at runtime.
examples: mapValues({ a: 1, b: 2 }, (value) => value * 2) // => { a: 2, b: 4 }
antiPatterns: No mapKeys. Rename keys outside the library.
Do not rely on inherited methods appearing in the result; the type lists keyof T, the runtime copies own enumerable keys only.

functions.name: pick
functions.signature: <T extends object, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, keys: readonly K[]): Pick<T, K>
functions.summary: Creates a new object with only the specified own keys.
antiPatterns: No path get() — only top-level keys

functions.name: omit
functions.signature: <T extends object, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, keys: readonly K[]): Omit<T, K>
functions.summary: Creates a new object without the specified keys.

functions.name: pickBy
functions.signature: <T extends object>(obj: T, predicate: (value: T[keyof T], key: keyof T) => boolean): Partial<T>
functions.summary: Creates a new object with entries that satisfy the predicate.
examples: pickBy({ a: 1, b: null }, (v) => v != null)

functions.name: omitBy
functions.signature: <T extends object>(obj: T, predicate: (value: T[keyof T], key: keyof T) => boolean): Partial<T>
functions.summary: Creates a new object without entries that satisfy the predicate.
examples: omitBy({ a: 1, b: null }, (v) => v == null)

functions.name: clone
functions.summary: Creates a shallow clone of a value.
examples: const copy = clone(obj); // nested refs shared
antiPatterns: Use cloneDeep when nested objects must be independent

functions.name: cloneDeep
functions.summary: Creates a deep clone (objects, arrays, Map, Set, Date, RegExp; handles cycles).
antiPatterns: No structuredClone polyfill claim — this is the library implementation

functions.name: cloneWith
functions.summary: Shallow clone with a customizer callback.

functions.name: cloneDeepWith
functions.summary: Deep clone with a customizer callback.
examples: cloneDeepWith({ a: { b: 1 } }, (val) => (typeof val === 'number' ? val * 2 : undefined))

functions.name: debounce
functions.signature: <T extends (...args: any[]) => any>(func: T, wait?: number, options?: DebounceOptions): DebouncedFunction<T>
functions.summary: Debounces a function; exposes cancel() and flush(). Options: leading, trailing, maxWait.

functions.name: throttle
functions.signature: <T extends (...args: any[]) => any>(func: T, wait?: number, options?: ThrottleOptions): ThrottledFunction<T>
functions.summary: Throttles a function to at most once per wait ms. Options: leading, trailing.

functions.name: noop
functions.summary: No-op function useful as a default callback.

functions.name: identity
functions.summary: Returns the first argument unchanged.

functions.name: once
functions.summary: Invokes func at most once after a successful call; retries if it throws.

functions.name: clamp
functions.signature: (value: number, min: number, max: number): number
functions.summary: Clamps value between min and max (order-independent bounds).
antiPatterns: No mean/range helpers. Use sum or sumBy for totals.

functions.name: delay
functions.summary: Resolves after the specified milliseconds.
